newsitem.title: UK: New UK cable giant backed by C&W shareholders.
newsitem.headline: New UK cable giant backed by C&W shareholders.

text.p: Shareholders in Cable and Wireless Plc on Thursday overwhelmingly backed the creation of Cable & Wireless Communications Group at an extraordinary general meeting.

The new group brings together Mercury Communications Ltd, the UK subsidiary of Cable & Wireless and three cable television units of NYNEX Corp and Bell Cablemedia Plc to form Britain's biggest cable company.

"This is a major milestone in the creation of our new company which, as the largest provider of integrated telecommunication and television entertainment services in the U.K., will be a powerfule force in the U.K. telecommunication market," said chief executive Richard Brown.
Cable & Wireless Communications, which has been valued by analyts at between 4.5-7.0 billion pounds, will serve about 1.2 million telephony customers and 580,000 cable television customers.

The company, which will float a 14.7 percent stake in London and New York in the next few weeks, hopes to win six million residential customers by 2001, offering a broad range of voice and data telecommunications services and multichannel and broadband services.
The initial offer period of the share offers in the new company will expire at 1330 GMT, April 25. The partial flotation is expected immediately following the close of the offers.
